chapter: Lee and Lester Young band remembered
title: Stokowski and the movie stars at the Capri
summary: Leopold Stokowski and many Hollywood actors came to the Capri to watch Leo and the dancers.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So who was the gray-haired man?

Leopold Stokowski. Figure that one out. Yeah, and you know who used to come in and sit right... (reserved seats; they were all reservations)...and sit right in front so they could watch Leo? Jack Benny and his wife, and Robert Taylor and Barbara Stanwyck. They'd come in

there three or four nights a week. George Raft used to come in with Betty Grable and dance around. John Carradine used to be hunched over the bar, listening -- he thought it was great. All kinds of actors.

I met a lot of great actors there. I met this one guy, Mark...I think his last name was Lawrence. Real pockmarked face. He used to play these real heavies in the Italian gangster pictures. He was a great guy. I met him... We were out... Right during the intermission, when I went out to get some air, and he was standing there. And he says, "Boy, youze guys really whoop it up, dontcha." He says, "I like that girl dancer"...
